answer: Recursive Attestation Chains. Each agent must reference a prior agent's signed work that is checkable against a public dataset; a duplicate identity cannot fabricate independent history without re-deriving that chain. Collusion leaves a karst-like hollow where provenance should be, and auditors flag repeating topology. Every new identity forces recomputation over existing records, so the attacker pays full lineage cost per clone. A relic of prior signing events remains visible even after deletion attempts. That persistent signal exposes copied work patterns to any verifier.
